status: normalized; execution results live in traces_results.json
evidence_class: source_documented (fixture text) + locally_observed (results); no profile is qualified

traces.title: Descendant escape and causal work completeness
traces.injected_fault: a supervisor process group spawns nested children; one child deliberately escapes via setsid (new session/process group).
traces.observation_oracle: enumerate actors through /proc: contained actors share the declared boundary pgid; the escaped actor has a different pgid. A denied/escaped attempt is an observed outcome, not a skipped variant.
traces.recovery_oracle: close admission, kill the declared boundary, enumerate survivors, reconcile the escaped actor through the separately approved harness cleanup identity, then verify the scope is empty.
traces.stop_condition: any actor running outside the promised boundary rejects completeness; any unrelated process affected is a safety stop; loss of actor/scope visibility yields unknown.
traces.negative_control: deliberately permit the setsid escape and require descendant_capture_complete to become false while the contained actors remain true.
traces.bounds: bounded sleeps (<=30s), unique temp dir, own process group, explicit cleanup trap.

traces.title: Parent death before registration
traces.injected_fault: kill creator B after native child creation returns but before the registration record is committed.
traces.observation_oracle: the child pid is alive, the creator is dead and registration is absent; the unresolved launch must be visible from native /proc state, not inferred from a missing response.
traces.recovery_oracle: a new epoch reconciles registered intent against live identities and terminates the still-unregistered child under policy; it must not launch a replacement before resolving the first launch.
traces.stop_condition: an unfenced worker performs work or the recovery policy loses a witnessed child rejects; unobservable creation/commit order yields unknown.
traces.negative_control: open the create-then-register gap and confirm that a registration-record-only oracle would wrongly report not_started while the orphan is live.
traces.bounds: own temp child, bounded sleep, explicit kill cleanup trap.

traces.title: Last handle and scope lifetime
traces.injected_fault: crash the broker while another actor retains a duplicated or inherited Job handle, or while a terminal descriptor is held open after W exits.
traces.observation_oracle: capture reference ownership transfers, native member state and termination events; broker death must not be inferred to mean last-handle closure or scope destruction.
traces.recovery_oracle: determine whether the scope survived and whether it can be reattached safely; releasing observer references happens after the evidence window.
traces.stop_condition: settlement while a required actor survives rejects; inability to distinguish which handle kept the scope alive yields unknown; harness cleanup before observation invalidates the cell.
traces.negative_control: deliberately retain one extra reference; it must remain visible and prevent premature settled status.
traces.unsupported_reason: requires an explicit ownership inventory of Job handles, pidfds, inherited descriptors and monitor references on a disposable native scope; no Windows Job-object route is authorized and WSL2 has no equivalent handle lifecycle to observe.

traces.title: Undrained terminal teardown
traces.injected_fault: stop the output consumer at output_blocked, then tear down the terminal host; a duplicated writer/reader is retained as the negative control.
traces.observation_oracle: record teardown call begin/return, each endpoint close cause, last complete output sequence and count, process exit evidence and scope emptiness; the consumer cannot be the only observer of the call that can block it.
traces.recovery_oracle: reconcile bounded output retention with the selected loss policy; a drained terminal has no missing acknowledged records and a truncated terminal has an explicit loss boundary and reason.
traces.stop_condition: watchdog-confirmed violation of the bounded teardown contract rejects; lost watchdog or uncertain blocking point yields unknown; unbounded memory growth while buffering is a safety stop.
traces.negative_control: retain a duplicated output writer/reader so all_clients_disconnected cannot be claimed; a harness-caused closure must be labeled local_close.
traces.bounds: bounded capture window under a hard timeout, private temp PTY/pipe, no host terminal attached; the host variant reads a bounded prefix before stalling.

traces.title: Signals and console event scope
traces.injected_fault: send a graceful termination signal to a process group while a child ignores it; an unrelated sentinel lives in a different session.
traces.observation_oracle: record API return, handler receipt, continuation heartbeat, native exit and final forced termination as distinct events; the unrelated sentinel must remain unaffected.
traces.recovery_oracle: after the graceful deadline, escalate against stable owned identities or scope membership, verify emptiness and account for actors beyond the declared signal scope.
traces.stop_condition: wrong-target delivery or unrelated sentinel death is a safety stop; failure to exit without proven observer completeness yields unknown.
traces.negative_control: the sentinel in a different session must survive and an ignoring target must not be recorded as exited merely because a signal was sent.
traces.bounds: own temp processes, bounded signal deadline, explicit SIGKILL cleanup trap.

traces.title: Atomic replacement crash cuts
traces.injected_fault: crash the writer at cuts around flush and replacement of generation A by generation B in the same directory.
traces.observation_oracle: reopening readers see only namespace-permitted states, generation A or generation B, with no torn or mixed bytes; preserve native result and file identity.
traces.recovery_oracle: before repair, inventory original/replacement names and contents, then select or quarantine; the witness generation must be recoverable and a lost response must not be equated with no effect.
traces.stop_condition: torn or mixed canonical content, or a forbidden live namespace gap, rejects; unknown crash ordering remains unknown.
traces.negative_control: a non-atomic copy-plus-delete fallback must be detected as a name gap and may never impersonate a successful atomic replacement.
traces.bounds: temp directory only, bounded repetitions, the crash kills only the writer's own process; host runs the non-crash application-visible variant.

traces.title: Failure domain and power interruption
traces.injected_fault: repeat the durability-relevant cuts for abrupt process death, guest reset, host reset and actual physical power interruption of the named devices.
traces.observation_oracle: record which power/reset domain actually failed, the last externally witnessed acknowledgment, and evidence that no graceful flush path ran; device/cache behavior is pinned or unknown.
traces.recovery_oracle: boot or remount through the frozen procedure, retain the first observed bytes before repair, verify generation/digest and application consistency.
traces.stop_condition: any promised acknowledged generation lost rejects that exact domain; apparatus uncertainty yields unknown; an unsafe device or unapproved destructive boundary is a safety stop.
traces.negative_control: a graceful shutdown is a control, never the injected crash; a simulated controller-flush failure is a separate synthetic fault.
traces.unsupported_reason: requires approved abrupt physical/VM reset apparatus, separately powered witnesses, exact storage/cache topology and a recoverable test image; human-gated and not available.

traces.title: Lock lifetime and mapped bypass
traces.injected_fault: terminate the lock owner, contend while release is delayed, and perform a raw/mapped write that bypasses the lock primitive while the lock is held.
traces.observation_oracle: record acquisition completion, native result/error, competing write attempts, overlapping writes and owner identity; a stale lock file's existence is recorded separately from a currently enforced native lock; the mapped bypass must be detected as outside the primitive's protection.
traces.recovery_oracle: a new owner re-acquires the native lock under a bounded policy and verifies fencing and canonical consistency before resuming; it must not assume authority because a PID is absent.
traces.stop_condition: two admitted writers or a false exclusivity claim rejects; no visibility of current lock ownership yields unknown.
traces.negative_control: a raw write outside the lock must be detected as a bypass and a stale marker must not be treated as ownership.
traces.bounds: single temp lock file, bounded hold, explicit cleanup trap; host variant is advisory-lock acquire/release only.

traces.title: PID reuse and stale process identity
traces.injected_fault: let the original process exit and be reaped, force a numeric PID reuse in an isolated PID namespace, then deliver stale-epoch messages to that numeric PID.
traces.observation_oracle: distinguish stable identity (starttime/pidfd) from the numeric PID; proof that reuse actually occurred is required, and churn without reuse is an untriggered cell, not a pass.
traces.recovery_oracle: stale messages cannot affect or settle the new process; reattach only when stable identity matches, otherwise record unknown and quarantine admission; no broad kill by name or PID is acceptable.
traces.stop_condition: stale cancellation reaches the unrelated sentinel or stale exit settles a new execution rejects; failure to trigger reuse yields unknown.
traces.negative_control: PID-only targeting must identify the wrong-target hazard without affecting any real process.
traces.bounds: isolated PID namespace, bounded reuse via ns_last_pid, no signal is ever sent to a reused PID.

traces.title: Disk full quota and delayed write failure
traces.injected_fault: exhaust byte space in a bounded filesystem between content write and flush, then attempt to publish generation B while generation A must survive.
traces.observation_oracle: every write has requested and actual lengths; flush/replace has its own result; no success is claimed from a completed buffered write; whether error reporting itself failed is captured.
traces.recovery_oracle: preserve A or a fully validated B; never accept a truncated B because a name exists; restore space only after recording the failing state and distinguish restored capacity from successful recovery.
traces.stop_condition: false durable acknowledgment or torn canonical data rejects; loss of independent error evidence yields unknown; spillover to non-disposable storage is a safety stop.
traces.negative_control: a truncated B plus the existence of the name must not be accepted as success, and the predecessor generation must remain.
traces.bounds: tmpfs size=16m mounted in memory, hard iteration cap, unmounted and deleted on exit; never writes host disk.

traces.title: Memory throttling without automatic death inference
traces.injected_fault: drive a bounded allocation workload under a hard address-space limit as a substitute for memory.high; cgroup v2 is read-only in this WSL2 target.
traces.observation_oracle: correlate actual allocation refusal, progress cadence and live scope; report the refusal even if execution later exits normally; missing counters are recorded as unknown, not zero.
traces.recovery_oracle: remove only the test pressure according to preregistration and determine whether work resumes; do not respawn under pressure and do not bill throttled wall time as CPU.
traces.stop_condition: a portable OOM classification without subtype evidence rejects; counter or clock coverage loss yields unknown; host pressure escaping the disposable domain is a safety stop.
traces.negative_control: the classifier must not infer death from absence and must not classify a progress stall as a memory failure.
traces.bounds: ulimit -v 64 MiB inside a subshell, timeout, no cgroup writes and no global OOM provocation.

traces.title: Memory refusal process kill and group kill
traces.injected_fault: hit memory.max under individual and group policies and provoke a bounded allocation-refusal path with explicit per-process/group limits.
traces.observation_oracle: record allocation outcomes, native memory events and process identities, which members died and whether the controller caused the death; multiple chronological outcomes are possible.
traces.recovery_oracle: account for survivor state and incomplete work before replay; an isolated killed child cannot leave a parent silently committing a partial result; group cleanup and settlement are verified separately.
traces.stop_condition: incorrect subtype or duplicate retry while survivors run rejects; global OOM outside the authorized scope is a safety stop; ambiguous cause of death yields unknown.
traces.negative_control: a harness-policy termination must be labeled as such rather than as native limit behavior.
traces.unsupported_reason: requires a private writable Linux memory controller (memory.max) and explicit OOM group policy; cgroup v2 is mounted read-only in this WSL2 dev/test target and provoking global OOM is a safety stop.

traces.title: Supervisor restart and stale owner race
traces.injected_fault: crash the owner before/after ownership registration and race an automatic restart with a manual start while delivering the old owner's delayed completion.
traces.observation_oracle: record every launch request, execution epoch, stable identity and admitted writer authority; stopped/active service state cannot replace native scope evidence.
traces.recovery_oracle: exactly one authorized owner may admit work for the intended generation, old epochs stay fenced and pending restart sources are reconciled.
traces.stop_condition: dual ownership or an accepted stale completion rejects; editing an unrelated service is a safety stop; missing activation visibility yields unknown, not quiescence.
traces.negative_control: an unfenced competitor that writes authority without the ownership lock must be detected as a second owner.
traces.bounds: flock-fenced single authority, bounded holds, own temp service processes and cleanup trap.

traces.title: Suspend resume and deadline semantics
traces.injected_fault: suspend across a deadline, resume after it, change wall time separately and reboot with a persisted deadline.
traces.observation_oracle: compare pre/post clock readings with explicit suspend/resume events, accounting for CLOCK_MONOTONIC versus CLOCK_BOOTTIME semantics and measurement uncertainty.
traces.recovery_oracle: expire once for elapsed semantics or retain the correct active budget, and reconcile after reboot using the approved epoch policy.
traces.stop_condition: missed or duplicate expiration outside tolerance rejects; a wrong clock or uncertain pause domain yields unknown; acting on the real system clock outside the disposable target is a safety stop.
traces.negative_control: a persisted monotonic number from an old boot must not be treated as a current deadline without conversion evidence.
traces.unsupported_reason: WSL2 cannot be reliably suspended/resumed, host suspend is human-gated and outside the disposable target, and the Owner's elapsed-versus-active deadline-semantics choice is not recorded.

traces.title: Network storage interruption and ambiguous commit
traces.injected_fault: drop requests before receipt and responses after effect, cut connectivity during write/flush/replacement/lock renewal, restart the server and recover with retained or lost volatile state.
traces.observation_oracle: capture request identity, protocol result when available, server evidence, client error and first authoritative post-reconnect state; a timeout is neither not_committed nor committed.
traces.recovery_oracle: verify generation/content against independent acknowledgment, detect changed server identity/verifier or lost locks and reacquire authority before writes resume.
traces.stop_condition: conflicting writers or false durability claims reject; no independent server observation yields unknown; a shared production volume is a safety stop.
traces.negative_control: a durable handle is not by itself proof of durable application content; a client page-cache read is not a server recovery observation.
traces.unsupported_reason: SMB/NFS are out of canonical scope (platform-floors D-028) and an isolated share/export with independent client and server witnesses is not available.

traces.title: Lost duplicated and reordered notifications
traces.injected_fault: remove a process exit notification, deliver it twice or after the next epoch, overrun an observation buffer and restart the observer while a worker exits.
traces.observation_oracle: sequence/epoch checks detect duplicates and gaps; authoritative native state resolves what it can and loss of observation coverage is explicit.
traces.recovery_oracle: reconcile native identities, canonical record and final accounting; if exact time or cause cannot be reconstructed, retain unknown even when eventual death is established.
traces.stop_condition: silent gap, false success, stale event accepted or unknown converted to zero rejects.
traces.negative_control: removing a notification must not produce the claim that the event never happened.
traces.unsupported_reason: requires an observation-transport harness that can drop, duplicate and reorder synthetic notifications while independent native queries remain available.

traces.title: Compatibility path and embedded host boundary
traces.injected_fault: launch native children through a compatibility shell with spaces, Unicode, leading dashes and case collisions, then cross a WSL native/Windows mount boundary and terminate the embedded host.
traces.observation_oracle: compare exact arguments, path identities, resulting filesystem route, terminal ownership, process scope and exit evidence; a successful shell command is not proof the intended native binary ran.
traces.recovery_oracle: preserve the same execution identity and canonical data route or reject unsupported reconnect; host closure must not silently change cancellation or persistence policy.
traces.stop_condition: unintended binary/path, profile substitution or inherited native qualification rejects; unknown translation yields unknown.
traces.negative_control: a successful shell command must not be accepted as proof that the intended native binary or storage route was exercised.
traces.unsupported_reason: requires separate MSYS2, Git Bash and embedded-terminal profile instances; only the WSL2 dev/test target exists in this environment.

traces.title: Permission and feature denial
traces.injected_fault: deny Job assignment, cgroup creation/delegation, clone3, pidfd access, lock acquisition, replacement or flush; include unavailable-feature and policy-denied variants.
traces.observation_oracle: record the native denial code, effective policy and presence/absence of partially created work; the adapter must not silently fall back to a weaker guarantee under a stronger label.
traces.recovery_oracle: reconcile partial resources, keep admission closed where the promised guarantee is unavailable, and report unsupported or unknown with the original evidence retained.
traces.stop_condition: undeclared fallback or work released outside the promised policy rejects; unapproved privilege escalation is a safety stop.
traces.negative_control: a present-but-policy-denied feature must not be recorded as a successful acquisition.
traces.unsupported_reason: requires disposable policy variants with exact security/configuration digests and explicit authorization for each local privilege or policy change; no test may disable production protections.

traces.title: Resource accounting completeness
traces.injected_fault: let a child run and exit between sampling intervals, kill the parent first, lose one counter sample and reset/recreate the scope.
traces.observation_oracle: report counter source, units, aggregation boundary, sampling interval and reset semantics; scope cumulative accounting is distinct from summed per-PID samples and from simultaneous group peaks.
traces.recovery_oracle: return bounded or unknown accounting where a delta cannot be recovered, preserve terminal costs separately and prevent zero substitution for a missing counter.
traces.stop_condition: double count, reset read as negative usage, incomplete capture represented as exact or a missing value represented as zero rejects.
traces.negative_control: reusing a scope name must not splice two counter epochs into one charge.
traces.unsupported_reason: requires a stable writable cgroup scope with native cumulative counter baselines; cgroup v2 is mounted read-only in this WSL2 target.

traces.title: Combined failures and oracle controls
traces.injected_fault: combine output backpressure with supervisor crash, disk-full with writer death, memory pressure with observer restart, response loss with lock-owner restart, and suspend/resume with cancellation at the deadline.
traces.observation_oracle: each combined fault has its own confirmation and causal order and the intentionally faulty controls must fail the corresponding oracle.
traces.recovery_oracle: settlement requires all relevant terminal, containment, ownership, accounting and durability predicates without one recovered component masking another.
traces.stop_condition: any violated mandatory invariant rejects; an ineffective fault or insensitive oracle invalidates the cell as unknown.
traces.negative_control: intentionally faulty adapters for false settlement, omitted flush, PID-only identity and notification-only completion must be flagged.
traces.unsupported_reason: the combined variant list must be preregistered and all component fixtures need independent evidence first; component coverage is incomplete.
